upstreamAdvisory.fixStatus: not fixed for gcc-12 in Debian; upstream fixed in GCC trunk by commit aaa8351f4d2e636f9680a1f0a8ebc2f0a60611e6 (2026-09-25, Jonathan Wakely, PR libstdc++/127656)
upstreamAdvisory.affectedCondition: use-after-free in __gnu_pbds detail::binary_heap erase_if: after reallocating the entry storage, the member pointer m_a_entries is left dangling (storage freed, new storage leaked). One-line fix adds `m_a_entries = new_entries;`.
upstreamAdvisory.affectedApi: __gnu_pbds::priority_queue (policy-based data structures, <ext/pb_ds/priority_queue.hpp>) backed by the binary_heap tag, when erase_if(pred) is invoked. NOT std::priority_queue (<queue>) — std::priority_queue has no erase_if and its underlying std heap algorithms are unrelated to pb_ds binary_heap_ internals.

findings.presenceEvidence: POSITIVELY ABSENT in every compiled C++ consumer shipped in the exact artifact. The vulnerable code is not in libstdc++.so at all: it lives only in the header <ext/pb_ds/detail/binary_heap_/erase_fn_imps.hpp> and is instantiated into a consumer's binary only if that consumer includes and instantiates __gnu_pbds binary_heap priority_queue erase_if. All compiled C++ consumers in the artifact were enumerated by a filesystem-wide libstdc++ DT_NEEDED scan (receipts libstdcxx-consumer-set.json, libstdcxx-consumers-final.txt): /usr/local/bin/node, apt frontends + libapt-pkg/libapt-private, and /workspace/node_modules/@img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64/lib/libvips-cpp.so.8.18.7. For each: zero 'pb_ds' strings (cve-102010-presence-probe.txt/probe2.txt), zero __gnu_pbds/binary_heap dynsym entries on the host-parsed ELF64 .dynsym of node, libstdc++ and libvips-cpp (dynsym-align-val-analysis.json), and zero 'stl_heap'/'binary_heap' strings in node. The V8 subtree that Node 24.21.0 (commit 955266bfdd854cd280dffd47548673914484e4c0) builds contains no reference to ext/pb_ds (source tree grep of deps/v8: no pb_ds include anywhere). This is a positive-absence proof at the consumer-binary level (byte strings + dynsym of the exact shipped binaries), not a libstdc++.so dynsym miss, and therefore is not the CR-04 defect: the CR-04 objection (a header-only template may be inlined into compiled consumers) is met by auditing the consumers themselves.
findings.reachabilityEvidence: Not needed once presence is disproven, and independently corroborated: the only runtime C++ consumer is node (process 'node'), which loads libstdc++ but instantiates no pb_ds code; the running processes are node (web/worker) and postgres (separate image, out of scope). Even the weakest residual consumer (libvips-cpp, loaded by no process in dev mode) carries zero pb_ds bytes. There is no code path by which the vulnerable erase_if instantiation exists in any executable page of this artifact.
findings.attackerControlledPrerequisite: Moot: the vulnerable operation is not present. For completeness — triggering requires C++ code calling erase_if on a __gnu_pbds binary_heap priority_queue with attacker-influenced contents; no such code exists in the artifact.

findings.residualRisk: LOW. The disposition rests on enumerated-consumer byte/symbol evidence of the exact artifact binaries. If a future image change ships a new compiled C++ binary that instantiates __gnu_pbds binary_heap erase_if, this disposition expires. Confidence HIGH for presence-absence (positive bytes/dynsym audit of every libstdc++ consumer); the audit did not rely on symbol absence from libstdc++.so.
findings.expiryRevalidationTrigger: earliest of: 7 days (local-dev); new image digest; libstdc++6/gcc-12 package version change; any change to the compiled C++ consumer set (new binary linking libstdc++.so.6); new upstream advisory; KEV status change.

findings.component: libstdc++6 aligned operator new(size_t, align_val_t) integer overflow (libsupc++/new_opa.cc)

environment.worker_command: nodemon --legacy-watch --polling-interval 1000 --watch apps/worker --watch packages --ext ts,json --exec node apps/worker/src/index.ts
environment.network_exposure: host binding is 127.0.0.1 only; container has no published port other than 3000->127.0.0.1
environment.application_subprocess_spawning: none - no child_process/exec/spawn reference exists in apps/** or packages/** (carried from PH-SEC-WO-007 §4; unchanged at parent head 5cf4c2f)

upstreamAdvisory.fixStatus: not fixed for gcc-12 in Debian; upstream fixed in GCC trunk by commit 59d235ffa5a69231eb42e5290d52dc8c90d28b7a (2026-09-23, Jonathan Wakely; Red Hat bug reference 2537811 per locked scanner evidence)
upstreamAdvisory.affectedCondition: operator new(size_t, align_val_t) rounds the size up to a multiple of the alignment ((sz + al - 1) & ~(al - 1)) before calling C11 aligned_alloc on targets compiled with _GLIBCXX_HAVE_ALIGNED_ALLOC and without _GLIBCXX_HAVE_POSIX_MEMALIGN. With sz near SIZE_MAX the addition wraps to a small value; aligned_alloc succeeds and returns a non-null pointer to an undersized region -> heap memory corruption in the caller.
upstreamAdvisory.overflowFormula: wraparound iff sz + align - 1 >= 2^64, i.e. sz >= 2^64 - (align - 1); for align=64 (the only alignment used by the artifact's sole aligned consumer): sz >= 2^64 - 63 = 18446744073709551553. A wrapped request then allocates (sz + 63) mod 64 bytes instead of sz.

findings.presenceEvidence: CONFIRMED PRESENT and confirmed to be the vulnerable variant: _ZnwmSt11align_val_t/_ZnamSt11align_val_t are exported by the shipped libstdc++.so.6.0.30 and the .so imports glibc 'aligned_alloc' (libstdcxx-allocator-imports.json; no posix_memalign import). Byte-level decode of _ZnwmSt11align_val_t (receipt libstdcxx-opnew-align-body.hex) shows the C11 rounding sequence lea rax,[rbx+rbp-1]; neg rbp; and rbp,rax ((sz+al-1) & ~(al-1)) at offset +0x2D followed by a call to glibc aligned_alloc — i.e. the exact code the upstream fix hardens is compiled in (the posix_memalign fast path from PR 113258 is NOT compiled in for gcc 12.2.0-14+deb12u1). node links this .so (ldd receipt artifact-identity.txt), so the vulnerable code is mapped into the running process.
findings.reachabilityEvidence: UNREACHABLE with any size that can trigger the overflow. Exhaustive PLT/call-site analysis of the exact shipped node binary (126,595,440 bytes): exactly one JUMP_SLOT relocation for _ZnamSt11align_val_t (GOT 0x6b55608, PLT stub 0x747010) and exactly 2 call sites to that stub (cve-95619-callsite-analysis.json), both inside v8::internal::OptimizingCompileTaskExecutor::EnsureInitialized() (symbol _ZN2v88internal29OptimizingCompileTaskExecutor17EnsureInitializedEv, 0xd71fc0..0xd72316). Source mapping at exact tag v24.21.0: deps/v8/src/compiler-dispatcher/optimizing-compile-dispatcher.cc:141-142 -> base::OwnedVector<OptimizingCompileTaskState>::New(max_tasks) -> std::make_unique<OptimizingCompileTaskState[]>(max_tasks); OptimizingCompileTaskState is alignas(PROCESSOR_CACHE_LINE_SIZE)=alignas(64) (optimizing-compile-dispatcher.h:29; PROCESSOR_CACHE_LINE_SIZE=64, common/globals.h:1025), so the call is operator new[](max_tasks * 64, align_val_t(64)). max_tasks = v8_flags.concurrent_turbofan_max_threads (DEFINE_UINT, default 4; flag-definitions.h:1181) or, if 0, NumberOfWorkerThreads() (node clamps to uv_available_parallelism()-1 min 1, src/node_platform.cc:88-93). n is a bounded small integer (default 4; CPU-derived pool, < 2^20 in any realistic host), so n*64 <= ~2^37 — more than 2^27 times below the 2^64-63 threshold. JS cannot influence max_tasks: it is a startup-only V8 flag/CLI value and a platform thread count, never a runtime JS-settable value (no reference in src/). The other compiled C++ consumers: apt/libapt carry zero align_val_t references (byte scan cve-95619-consumers.txt); libvips-cpp.so.8.18.7 has exactly one _ZnamSt11align_val_t call site at .text 0x403ab3 with constant size argument (mov esi,4) — cannot wrap — and libvips-cpp is loaded by no running process in the local-dev runtime (sharp is next's optional image-optimizer, used only by 'next start' production image optimization; compose runs next dev --webpack; no app import of sharp or next/image: sharp-libvips-exposure.json, libvips-cpp-aligned-new-callsite-analysis.json). The application's JS/TS surface cannot call a C++ operator; and the only C++ code that reaches the operator does so with a bounded, non-attacker-derived size. cppgc's aligned Allocate entry points (DEFINED dynsym symbols) do not call global aligned operator new at all — they route to the Oilpan PageBackend linear-allocation buffer (object-allocator.cc OutOfLineAllocateImpl), so the DEFINED cppgc symbols are name-coincidence, not calls.
findings.attackerControlledPrerequisite: an input path causing a compiled consumer to pass sz >= 2^64 - 63 to operator new(size_t, align_val_t). Positively disproven: the artifact's only aligned-new caller passes max_tasks*64 with max_tasks bounded by startup flags/thread counts; no JS-reachable API influences it; no other consumer calls aligned new with any size that can wrap (libvips: constant 4; apt: no calls).
findings.privilegePrerequisite: none (not applicable; also note container runs as node uid 1000 with no capabilities)

findings.residualRisk: LOW-MEDIUM. Vulnerable library code is confirmed mapped into the running node process; safety rests on (a) the complete enumeration of aligned-new call sites in the exact shipped node binary via PLT relocation analysis — the import exists precisely because calls go through the PLT; a same-binary inlined implementation of aligned operator new would not import the symbol, and a source search of the exact Node v24.21.0 tag for align_val_t finds only the cppgc path that does not call global aligned new, matching the binary — and (b) bounded startup-only sizes. Any Node/V8 upgrade or any new native module in the image expires this disposition. Confidence HIGH for the enumerated path; no path from JavaScript reaches the operator with attacker-controlled size.
findings.expiryRevalidationTrigger: earliest of: 7 days (local-dev); new image digest; node/V8 major or build change; libstdc++6/gcc-12 package version change (a Debian fix would move the row to FIXED); any new compiled C++ binary or native addon linking libstdc++.so.6 in the image; new upstream advisory; KEV status change.
